title: U.S. House · Illinois's 11th District
area: A sprawling district stretching from Chicago's southwest suburbs through Aurora, Joliet and Naperville to Bloomington in central Illinois.

context.text: Incumbent Bill Foster ran unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Democratic primary. Jeffrey Walter defeated Tedora Brown, Charlie Kim and Mike Pierce in the Republican primary. Ballotpedia calculated the district's Cook Partisan Voter Index as D+6, based on the 2020 and 2024 presidential elections.

summary.text: Bill Foster is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election to Illinois's 11th District. A physicist who co-founded a theater-lighting company and later worked as a particle-accelerator designer at Fermilab, he first served in the U.S. House from 2008 to 2011 and has represented the 11th District since 2013. He serves on the House Financial Services and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Graduated from the University of Wisconsin and received a doctorate in physics from Harvard University.
At age 19, he and his younger brother co-founded Electronic Theatre Controls, Inc., a theater-lighting manufacturer; Ballotpedia lists his involvement with the company as spanning 1975 to 2007.

Worked as a high-energy physicist and particle-accelerator designer at Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory (Fermilab) from 1990 to 2006. According to his House biography, he was on the team that discovered the top quark and led teams that designed and built facilities including the Antiproton Recycler Ring.
Represented Illinois's 14th District in Congress from 2008 to 2011, before being elected to the newly drawn 11th District in 2012 and taking office in 2013.
Serves on the House Financial Services Committee, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Financial Institutions, and on the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee.

His House biography says he helped create reforms in the financial services and housing markets after the Great Recession, including the Dodd-Frank Act, and describes him as the only PhD physicist in Congress.

In the 118th Congress he was appointed to the House Bipartisan Task Force on Artificial Intelligence by Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries and was named to the House Select Subcommittee on the Coronavirus.
According to his House biography, he lives in Naperville with his wife, Aesook, also a physicist, and has two adult children; his father was a civil rights lawyer.

priorities.text: Says every individual should have the right to live free from discrimination, a priority he traces to his father's work as a civil rights lawyer who wrote much of the Civil Rights Act of 1964's enforcement language.
priorities.quote: As the son of a Civil Rights lawyer who wrote much of the enforcement language of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, this issue is a top priority for me.

priorities.text: Supports workers' right to collectively bargain and says he will oppose federal efforts to weaken organizing rights.
priorities.quote: I proudly support the rights of workers to collectively bargain for better wages and better benefits, and I am proud that Illinois became the first state to protect those rights in our state's constitution.

positions.summary: Supports Israel's right to defend itself while saying it must act in accordance with the rules of war, and calls for more support for civilians harmed on both sides of the conflict.
positions.quote: I support Israel's right to defend itself from heinous terrorism that endangers innocent civilians, but they must do so in accordance with the rules of war that democracies must strive to follow.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

summary.text: Jeffrey (Jeff) Walter is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 11th District. Describing himself as a retired U.S. Navy Master Chief Petty Officer, a former Accenture senior manager and the current mayor of Elburn, he won the March 2026 Republican primary. He says he is running on fiscal responsibility, public safety, veterans' health care and infrastructure investment.

background.text: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection biography, he describes himself as a retired U.S. Navy Master Chief Petty Officer (E-9) with more than three decades of experience across leadership, public service and technology consulting.

According to his Ballotpedia biography, he worked as a senior manager at Accenture, where he says he led over $36 million in IT programs including 13 generative-AI proof-of-concepts and cloud and data migrations, especially in healthcare and telecommunications.
Shaw Local describes him as a retired IT consultant who served as an Elburn village trustee before becoming village president (mayor); it listed his age as 65 in March 2026.

As mayor of Elburn, Illinois, he says he has championed smart growth, regional collaboration, infrastructure investment and public safety, and modernized village governance through long-term strategic planning.
Won the four-candidate Republican primary for Illinois's 11th District on March 17, 2026, and faces incumbent Bill Foster in the general election.

priorities.text: Points to his record as mayor of modernizing infrastructure, balancing budgets and strengthening public safety in Elburn as evidence of results-driven leadership.
Says he brings a practical, centrist approach to fiscal responsibility, low taxes and strategic growth for the district.
priorities.quote: I bring practical, centrist leadership to Illinois' diverse 11th District, blending suburban prosperity, farmland, and tech innovation. I am committed to fiscal responsibility, low taxes, and strategic growth—focusing on what works, not politics.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to fiscal responsibility and low taxes.
